claims.claim: A newly admitted ordinary REMEDIATION RUN persists one exact bounded predecessor identity that binds source RUN id, source REVIEW id, selected finding id, and reviewed SHA to the same canonical lineage used for admission.
Approved-remediation execution and direct-candidate acceptance persist the same predecessor identity shape and derive it from canonical resolution rather than caller assertion or heuristic search.

Deterministic mismatch regressions prove inconsistent source RUN, REVIEW, finding, or reviewed SHA in a predecessor-bearing lineage fails closed during canonical publication/lineage validation with no fallback reconstruction or publication.

Historical REMEDIATION lineage without the new predecessor metadata remains readable and preserves its established single-finding validation/publication behavior without artifact migration or mutation.
A new valid single-finding predecessor-bearing REMEDIATION lineage preserves the existing DELTA review and safe-publication behavior after exact predecessor validation.

A new predecessor-bearing lineage whose exact source REVIEW contains multiple findings cannot publish on the basis of one selected finding's DELTA PASS and fails closed without auto-selecting, ordering, merging, or renaming siblings.
Unified State regressions prove both legacy and predecessor-bearing REMEDIATION RUNs remain observable with unchanged next-action taxonomy and no new mutation or finding-selection authority.
The implementation changes no REVIEW/REMEDIATION semantic schema, Executor prompt contract, ResultPackage schema, REPAIR semantics, retry/reroute behavior, or historical artifact contents.
